headline: Genetic and single-cell data converge on candidate disease genes and targets
label: Mendelian Randomization Target Prioritization
summary: Public GWAS, pQTL and single-cell datasets are being reanalyzed to nominate genetically supported candidate genes and drug targets.
synthesis: The dominant thread is prioritization of candidate genes and targets by layering genetic causal inference onto transcriptomic and single-cell data. Several items use Mendelian randomization with colocalisation and SMR-HEIDI, including the drugMR Nextflow pipeline built on GWAS and pQTL summary statistics and proteome-wide MR in coronary artery disease, which yields 29 candidate proteins, 17 newly linked to CAD. Proteome-wide MR also prioritizes MMP8 in Parkinson's disease. Other items pair scRNA-seq or CITE-seq with bulk cohorts to localize signals to cell types, such as oligodendrocyte-associated ANKIB1 in Alzheimer disease, monocyte-associated ANPEP in aortic dissection, and a monocyte-enriched stroke endotype. A reanalysis of six mouse AD scRNA-seq datasets reports 301 DE genes, mostly upregulated innate immune and interferon genes. The UC study is explicitly hypothesis-generating.
